rationale: Full official PMC reader collection screened. Member “Knowledge of population of Kyrgyzstan about the Mediterranean diet as a preventive factor against stroke and heart diseases” is a 280-person stroke/control questionnaire that mentions olive oil/olives but is neither PD nor apathy and does not specify refined oil. Separate member “Apathy is associated with disruption to distinct, large-scale white matter networks” studies apathy/MRI in 331 cerebral small-vessel-disease patients and has no olive-oil exposure. Collection-level lexical collision only; no member links the candidate exposure to the endpoint.

Entire FEBS Open Bio 2025 Posters collection body was screened in the official PMC reader and Wiley publisher version; Salford repository copy of the complete 15(Suppl 2):67–527 issue was also searchable. No olive oil, apathy, refined olive, or amotivation occurrence in member content; the only “olive” hit is an institutional affiliation (“University Institute of Research in Olive Groves and Olive Oils”). No relevant exposure/endpoint submatch.

Full official PMC reader collection screened (50th European Society of Human Genetics Conference: Posters). One member on PCSK9 p.Arg357His transgenic mice reports postprandial lipid response after olive-oil gavage; a separate Kleefstra-syndrome case abstract mentions absence of apathy. These are distinct members, no human PD cohort, no refined-oil specification, and no oil/apathy connection. Collection-level lexical collision only.

Full official PMC reader collection screened (Poster Session I, December 8, 2014). A 60-youth randomized fish-oil study used olive oil as placebo; a separate late-life-depression poster studied apathy-related motivation in 24 older adults with depression and 23 controls. The abstracts are unrelated and do not study refined oil, PD, or an olive-oil/apathy association.

Entire official PMC reader collection reviewed (Poster Session II, December 10, 2013). Separate members include a 56-participant youth fish-oil trial with olive-oil placebo and a methylphenidate study measuring apathy/anhedonia in depressed patients (plus an unrelated apathy/amotivation case). The oil appears as comparator in a different member; no olive-oil/apathy association, PD population, or refined-oil claim.

Full official PMC poster-session collection body reviewed. Member PB02-S09 tests extra-virgin olive-oil phenol hydroxytyrosol as an acute strategy after ischemic stroke; a separate normal-pressure hydrocephalus imaging member describes mild apathy among presenting symptoms. Different members and exposure/outcome contexts; no refined olive oil, Parkinson cohort, or oil/apathy association.

Full official PMC body of the 24th European Congress on Obesity abstract collection reviewed. Olive oil occurs in a study/dietary-pattern context (including extra-virgin olive oil); the sole apathy occurrence is a general obesity-diagnosis/coding discussion, not a measured participant endpoint or oil exposure. No refined-oil/apathy result, PD cohort, or linked study.
